title: Full Walkthrough: Writing & Using Skills — Nick Nisi and Zack Proser
talk_summary: A workshop on authoring Claude-style 'skills' (folder + SKILL.md with YAML front matter, optional scripts/references) as portable, composable units of agent instructions. Key mechanisms: descriptions as routing rules, progressive disclosure via reference files, deterministic script interpolation, confidence-scored clarification loops, and eval harnesses comparing with/without skill.

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep SKILL.md small and point to sub-files (e.g. testing.md, scoring rubric, per-framework migration docs) that the model only loads when relevant, instead of bloating always-loaded CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're doing like a scoring ... load the scoring rubric and read through that ... If we're not doing scoring, you don't have to load that

takeaways.technique: Deterministic script interpolation for known data
takeaways.what_they_do: Use bang-backtick script calls so the harness executes a command (e.g. git log) and injects exact output, rather than letting the model guess and re-derive it across retries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're not saying go grab the latest commits ... You're saying here are the latest 10 commits in the exact format that I expect

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the task with and without the skill, grade with a rubric, and fail if the skill version scores lower or below a threshold; re-run as models change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will load Claude without the skill and ask it to do a task and then load it with a skill and then it kind of has like a rubric
takeaways.numbers: claims ~30% accuracy drop from over-prescription (self-described as made-up numbers); threshold ~80-90% pass

takeaways.what_they_do: Prefer a few hard constraints ('never be vague', 'every finding cites file+line+commit') over long prescriptive step lists, which they found can hurt performance.
Skill computes a confidence score across dimensions (problem clarity, goal, success criteria, scope) and loops asking the user/agent questions until above threshold before starting work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's going to ask me uh some more things ... now I'm at 96 out of 100. So it understands what I want

takeaways.what_they_do: Spawn sub-agents with their own context window to do review/feedback loops and report back a problem list, keeping the main task's context clean.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I kick off a sub agent to go do those reviews and then it just reports back like there I found these problems
